newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila may curb forex options to stem speculation.
newsitem.headline: Manila may curb forex options to stem speculation.

text.p: The Philippine central bank said on Friday it was considering restricting foreign exchange options transactions to prevent their use in speculation against the peso.
"If we find that the options are also being used for speculation, we may have to include them in the prior approval requirement," deputy governor Alberto Reyes told Reuters.

While the options market was still a "negligible market", Reyes said it might be used as an alternative channel by speculators after the central bank restricted Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) contracts for three months.

The central bank on Tuesday effectively banned onshore banks from engaging in forward selling of dollars on a non-delivery basis, after it found out that the growing NDF contracts had exacerbated the recent speculative pressure on the peso.
Tuesday's memorandum said NDF offers must first be approved by the central bank. Central bank governor Gabriel Singson earlier said he was not inclined to approve any request.
The study on the options was expected to be completed by next week, and the monetary authorities would decide whether to include options in the same memorandum, Reyes said.
Reyes, however, said the bank had no intention of stifling the fledgling derivatives market.
"We are not going to restrict the whole derivatives market," Reyes said. The central bank started allowing derivatives trading two years ago.
"As far as we are concerned, we are not looking at other forms of derivatives which might be used for speculation," he added.
At present, it has granted derivatives licences to eight local and foreign banks.
The derivatives market is still small. Few Filipino corporations used derivatives to hedge their dollar positions, traders said.
Bankers Association of the Philippines president Deogracias Vistan, in a separate interview, said he welcomed the move to restrict the NDF, but expressed reservations on the plan to restrict options.
"That's not a factor (in speculation)," Vistan told reporters.
